title: Introducing Lists
objective: Create a list of related items and read individual elements using positive and negative index positions.

sourceAlignment.title: Python Crash Course, 3rd Edition
sourceAlignment.author: Eric Matthes
sourceAlignment.note: Alignment metadata only. Lesson prose and exercises are original Code Forge material.

paragraphs: A list stores a sequence of related values in a single variable. You build one by placing items inside square brackets and separating them with commas, like forge_crew = ["Talia", "Rook", "Sable"]. Lists can hold any type of value, and the items keep the order you gave them.

Every item in a list has an index — a numbered position Python uses to find it. Indexing starts at 0, so the first item in forge_crew is forge_crew[0], the second is forge_crew[1], and so on. Asking for an index that does not exist raises an IndexError.

Python also lets you count backward from the end of a list using negative indices. forge_crew[-1] is always the last item and forge_crew[-2] is the second-to-last. This works no matter how long the list is, which is handy when you don't know its exact length.
explanation.rule: List indices start at 0 from the front, and -1 from the back — forge_crew[0] is the first item and forge_crew[-1] is the last.

examples.title: Building a Roster
examples.note: forge_crew[0] reads the first item; forge_crew[-1] reads the last item without needing to know the list's length.

examples.title: Index Out of Range
examples.code:
colors = ["red", "gold"]
print(colors[1])
# colors[5] would raise IndexError - there is no third item
examples.note: Every index has to point at a position that actually exists in the list.

checks.question: What is the index of the first item in a list?

feedback.correct: Correct — Python list indices start counting at 0.
feedback.incorrect: Not quite. The very first item sits at index 0.

checks.question: Given squad = ["Nyx", "Bram", "Odele"], what does squad[-1] return?

feedback.correct: Correct — -1 always points at the last item in the list.
feedback.incorrect: Negative indices count backward from the end, so -1 is the last item.

assignment.title: Squad Report
assignment.brief: Write squad_report(members) that prints the squad leader (the first member) and the rear guard (the last member).
requirements: Access the first member using index 0.
Access the last member using a negative index.
Print "Rear guard: {name}" for the last member.
assignment.starterCode:
def squad_report(members):
    # Print the leader (first member) and rear guard (last member).
    pass

squad_report(["Nyx", "Bram", "Odele", "Fen"])
assignment.solutionCode:
def squad_report(members):
    leader = members[0]
    rear = members[-1]
    print(f"Leader: {leader}")
    print(f"Rear guard: {rear}")

squad_report(["Nyx", "Bram", "Odele", "Fen"])
